title: What Rudeness Does to the Mind
text:
In a series of experiments published in 2007, Christine Porath and Amir Erez tested what a short moment of rudeness does to people's performance. In the first study, the experimenter, the authority figure in that setting, made demeaning remarks to participants as they arrived. In a control condition, the experimenter behaved normally.

Afterward, all participants solved anagrams and were asked to come up with as many uses as they could for a brick, a standard test of creativity. Those who had been treated rudely solved fewer anagrams and produced fewer and less creative ideas. In a second study the rudeness came from a professor whom participants met on their way to the lab, someone with no role in the task, with similar effects.

The researchers also gave participants a chance to help someone during the session, and people who had just experienced rudeness were less likely to do so. Porath and Erez found that rudeness disrupted people's thinking, pulling their attention away from the task.
lesson: A single curt remark can lower people's thinking and generosity for the rest of the day. Leaders who are rude pay for it in their team's work.
source: Porath, C. L., and Erez, A. (2007). Does rudeness really matter? The effects of rudeness on task performance and helpfulness. Academy of Management Journal, 50(5), 1181-1197.
